title: Embedding endpoint: variance attenuation via stride-aware micro-batches and kernel dispatch tuning
creator: Marcus Chen
description:
Background: Recent customer reports and internal dashboards show elevated p99s for the embeddings endpoint under mixed-size requests. Existing work on opportunistic coalescing and fingerprint backfill reduced average latency but we still see high variance and occasional long tails when a few large sequences or quantized fallback kernels are scheduled in the same micro-batch.

Goal: Reduce p99 and p999 tail events for embeddings by 30-50% across key workloads while keeping median latency and throughput within 5% of baseline. Approach focuses on two complementary fronts: 1) request-side batching improvements (stride-aware micro-batches and token-span bucketing) to reduce variance introduced by multinomial sequence lengths, and 2) kernel dispatch and shim tuning (soft preemption, single-request kernel shimming, and quant-fallback hysteresis) to prevent single large requests or quant fallbacks from elongating micro-batches.

Proposed scope:
- Design and implement a stride-aware batching policy that groups requests by token-span distribution rather than only sequence length or arrival time. This uses a lightweight histogram fingerprint per request to create micro-batches with lower internal variance.
- Add a variance attenuation layer in the coalescer that limits the maximum allowed token-span delta inside a micro-batch and opportunistically pads small requests within latency SLOs.
- Implement soft preemption in the kernel dispatcher: when a request is predicted to cause kernel slow-path (quantized fallback or long KV cache warm), it can be preempted to a separate fast-path worker or scheduled as a dedicated micro-batch depending on remaining capacity.
- Kernel shim: introduce a single-request kernel shimming mode that routes heavy requests to an isolated execution lane for up to N tokens to avoid blocking mixed micro-batches.
- Metrics and experiments: create synthetic and production shadow experiments to measure p50/p95/p99/p999 and throughput. Add a dashboard tile showing micro-batch internal variance, preemption rate, and shim utilization.

Success criteria:
- p99 reduction >= 30% and p999 reduction >= 20% on mixed-size internal workload and two customer repro workloads.
- No regression >5% in median latency or token/sec throughput.
- Rollout can be toggled with per-customer policy and a canary that monitors error rates and cost delta.

Risks:
- Over-aggressive bucketing can increase median latency due to padding; mitigate with latency budget guardrails and telemetry to auto-tune padding thresholds.
- Preemption adds complexity to kernel scheduling; unit tests and staged canary required.
- Edge cases for extremely large requests may require fallbacks to dedicated capacity (Dedicated customers).

Artifacts & links:
- Design doc (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/stride-aware-batching-design
- Initial perf proof-of-concept PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1834
- Regression dashboard (internal): https://dash.redwood.ai/d/embeddings/variance-attenuation

Implementation plan (high level):
1) Week 1: Prototype stride histogram fingerprint and offline clustering against production traces.
2) Week 2: Implement variance attenuation in coalescer and add unit tests + benchmark harness.
3) Week 3: Kernel shim + soft preemption proof-of-concept; synth load tests.
4) Week 4: Canary rollout to 5% traffic with shadow metrics and cost tracking.
5) Week 5: Evaluate, tune thresholds, and expand rollout to 50% then GA.

Notes on measurements: use end-to-end request timestamps at ingress and egress, micro-batch composition logs, kernel execution events, and per-token duration. Track the distribution of token-span deltas within each micro-batch and correlate with tail events.
acceptance_criteria: Automated test coverage for stride histogram generation and coalescer policy
Dashboard tiles for micro-batch variance and shim/preempt metrics visible in Console
p99 improved by >= 30% on benchmark suite and two customer repros
Canary rollout controls and rollback playbook documented
PRs merged for runtime, coalescer, and dispatcher changes
